title: A first summit — and the start of something ongoing
excerpt: More than 60 of you joined us. THANK YOU for being part of our first edition and helping bring this community to life!
body:
Office Managers make a huge difference in how it feels to work at a company.
Last Friday, we brought them together for a day dedicated to them.

The first-ever Office Impact Summit at DB55 was about recognizing that contribution and creating space for Office, Facilities, and Workplace Experience professionals to connect, share ideas, and build a community.

title: Q1 Community Coffee Meetup
excerpt: A quarterly meetup for workplace professionals to connect, share ideas and shape better workplaces. Theme and agenda coming soon.
body:
The first Office Impact Community Meetup is for the people who run the workplace and shape how it feels.

Expect practical conversations, fresh ideas and time to connect with peers. More details, including the theme and agenda, will be shared soon.

title: Lost in translation: working across cultures
excerpt: Multinational offices can contain very different assumptions about directness, silence, feedback and what 'normal' looks like.
body:
A workplace can hold dozens of nationalities and just as many expectations about communication. Direct feedback can feel efficient to one colleague and confrontational to another; silence can signal agreement, disagreement or respect depending on context.

Office and workplace professionals often hear about these frictions early. That gives the role a practical influence on how teams understand each other and how culture is experienced day to day.

title: The right network can make the job easier
excerpt: People in office and workplace roles wear many hats. A peer network gives them somewhere to test ideas, share suppliers and ask the questions that are hard to answer alone.
body:
Office, facilities and workplace roles are unusually broad. One day can involve suppliers, events, wellbeing, budgets, culture, maintenance and employee questions.

A useful professional community does not need to produce another stream of generic content. It can simply connect people who understand the role, creating a place to exchange practical approaches and trusted recommendations.
